evals.prompt: I'm writing my own software audio mixer in C that sums many playing sounds into one output buffer for the sound card. Right now I add each sound's 16-bit samples directly into the 16-bit output buffer and when several loud sounds play at once I get a horrible loud burst of noise. Also, when a sound starts or its volume changes, I hear a sharp click. How should I structure the mixing and volume handling to fix both?
assertions: Recommends accumulating the mix in floating-point (deinterleaved/planar 32-bit float) rather than summing directly in the integer output format, then scaling to fit and converting to the device integer format only at the end
Explains that the burst comes from integer overflow/wraparound and that float accumulation tolerates sums outside [-1,1]
States that gain/volume changes must be ramped gradually over many samples (on the order of tens of milliseconds) rather than snapped, and the ramp advances per sample (not once per block)

evals.prompt: My game's audio render callback occasionally produces audible clicks and dropouts, especially the first time a new sound type plays or when the game is busy. Inside the callback I currently take a mutex to read the list of active sounds, malloc a temporary scratch buffer for mixing, and sometimes printf when a sound finishes. What is wrong with this and how should the callback and the game-thread-to-audio-thread communication be structured?
assertions: States the audio callback must never lock/take a mutex, allocate or free (malloc/free), do I/O (printf/file/network), or otherwise do unbounded/blocking work on the audio path
Says all buffers and voice state must be preallocated and pre-touched/pinned at startup so the first callback does not page-fault, and that the 'first time' glitch is a first-touch page fault

Says the game thread should hand work to the audio thread via a lock-free (single-producer/single-consumer) command queue drained at the top of the render block instead of sharing/mutating state under a lock

evals.prompt: In my C audio engine each sound asset can be at a different sample rate than my 44100 Hz mixer, and I also want per-sound pitch/playback-speed control. My current approach uses a float variable that I increment to track my read position in the source, and long ambient loops slowly drift out of tune over a minute or two. How should I do the sample-rate conversion and pitch, and why is my long sound going out of tune?
assertions: Describes reading the source with a single fractional per-voice playback step where step = (src_rate / mix_rate) * pitch, so one step handles both rate conversion and pitch/speed together, and interpolating (linear by default) between bracketing source samples
States the read cursor/position must be kept in double (or fixed-point), not float, because accumulating the fractional position in float drifts/loses precision over long sounds

evals.prompt: My audio system dynamically allocates a new voice struct with malloc every time a sound plays and frees it when the sound ends, and it hands the caller a raw pointer to that voice so they can change its volume later. Under heavy action the audio thread stutters, and sometimes changing a sound's volume affects a completely different sound. How should I manage the voices instead?
assertions: Recommends a fixed-size preallocated voice pool (cap concurrency at MAX_VOICES, no per-play malloc/free on the audio thread) so the mix loop's worst case is bounded
Says to hand out an opaque handle containing a slot index plus a generation counter (validated before use) instead of a raw pointer, so stale references to a recycled voice are detected

Says that when the pool is full you steal the least important voice (ranked by priority first, then loudness/age) and must ramp the stolen/stopped voice's gain to zero before reusing its slot rather than cutting it instantly
